topic.title: settle ho jao
topic.claim: 'Settle ho jao' doesn't mean marriage or a house. It means become someone we can stop worrying about.
topic.moment: You list the promotion, the flat, the savings, and mummy still sighs, 'bas ab settle ho jao.'

turn.believed: Settling down means the specific checklist: marriage, house, stable job.
turn.actually: The checklist is just a proxy. What they actually want is to stop lying awake about you.

topic.because: They can't carry the worry forever and they know it. Every milestone they name is really them asking for permission to relax about you before they run out of time.
topic.payoff: 'Settle ho jao' was never about marriage or a house. It was them asking when they can finally stop worrying.
topic.feeling: the realisation that their nagging is just fear wearing a to-do list
topic.villain: the arrangement that makes a parent's peace conditional on your milestones
topic.behaviour: parents keep moving the 'settle down' goalpost no matter what you achieve
topic.mechanism: the milestones are a stand-in for the real ask: permission to stop worrying about you
topic.group: adults tired of the 'settle down' pressure
topic.send_to: a friend who fights with their parents about 'settling down'
topic.why_now: wedding-season visits where the 'settle' talk restarts
